verdict.rationale: Docs clearly describe container tags as hard namespace boundaries scoped per user/agent/app, with code examples (containerTag: "user_123") and explicit statements that memories in one tag are never returned by searches scoped to another. However, this relies on developers correctly setting containerTag on every write/search call rather than enforced platform-level tenant isolation, and there's a community report suggesting a related MCP deployment had no auth (URL-as-key), raising questions about access-control rigor. missing for 10: independent/hands-on verification of leak-proof isolation under adversarial conditions, and clarity on default behavior if containerTag is omitted.
